speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a rash on your scalp and forehead; to better understand your condition, how long have you had these symptoms, and have you noticed any scaling, crusting, or hair loss?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cradle Cap (Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis).

*Note: While the patient's age and family history of psoriasis are relevant, the presentation of red, scaly rash on the scalp and forehead in a 3-month-old is characteristic of seborrheic dermatitis. If symptoms persist or worsen, I would request images of the affected areas to rule out tinea capitis.*
